affectedCopies: Prisma-to-EA current-state data-model mirror (EaConformanceIssue rows of type growth-without-disposition / payload-anatomy)
Backlog (fingerprinted corrective items with source data-growth)

privacyAssessment.dataSubjectRights: not-applicable — rows hold table names and byte/row counts from pg_class and pg_stat_user_tables; no row content, no identifiers of people
privacyAssessment.reviewDisposition: No data-subject workflow is introduced. The sample table is itself declared telemetry-bounded with a 90-day purge window in the schema tag, so the steward's own telemetry is governed by the same mechanism it enforces.

migration.name: 20260909230000_table_growth_sample
migration.backfill: Additive: one new, initially empty table with two indexes. No existing row, column or enum is touched. The first nightly run populates it; detectors need two samples before a growth rate exists and PERSISTENT_NIGHTS (3) before a backlog item is filed, so nothing is asserted from a single night.
migration.rollback: Forward-only; a corrective migration would drop the table. Nothing else references it.

changes.lifecycleDisposition: Declared in the schema: /// @dpf lifecycle=telemetry-bounded retention=90d timeAxis=sampledAt. The retention sweep reads that declaration from the catalog and purges samples older than 90 days; industry floors do not lengthen the telemetry bucket beyond one year.

fields.reason: Physical table name from pg_class — the join key to the model's catalog declaration and its EA data_object element.
Row growth on the model's declared time axis; the input the growth-without-disposition detector thresholds on.
The disposition the schema declared at sample time, so a finding can be reproduced after a tag changes.
